findings.title: Define temporal identity with exact integer coordinates
findings.detail:
Extend _key at :639 using exact-type dispatch, leaving the non-temporal keys unchanged. Use attoseconds as the common integer coordinate. The fixed-unit factors are W=604800×10^18, D=86400×10^18, h=3600×10^18, m=60×10^18, s=10^18, ms=10^15, us=10^12, ns=10^9, ps=10^6, fs=10^3, as=1. Convert the raw NumPy integer to Python int before multiplication.

The keys are: date → ('date', value.toordinal()); naive datetime/Timestamp/datetime64 → ('datetime','naive',coordinate); aware datetime/Timestamp → ('datetime','aware',coordinate); fixed duration → ('duration',length). A Timestamp coordinate is int(value.asm8.view('i8')) multiplied by the factor for value.unit. Its aware asm8 integer already represents UTC; do not subtract the offset again or use .value, which demands nanoseconds and can overflow. A datetime coordinate is wall_us×10^12 when naive, or (wall_us−offset_us)×10^12 when aware, where wall_us=(value.replace(tzinfo=None)−datetime(1970,1,1))//timedelta(microseconds=1), and offset_us=value.utcoffset()//timedelta(microseconds=1). This incorporates fold and provider offsets without constructing an out-of-range UTC datetime. Ignore a naive datetime's fold.

For np.datetime64, read (unit,multiple)=np.datetime_data(value.dtype), then n=int(value.view('i8'))×int(multiple). Fixed units use n×factor. Y means January 1 of year 1970+n; M means the first day of year 1970+n//12, month n%12+1. Compute days from 1970-01-01 with Python integers and the proleptic Gregorian calendar: subtract one from y for January/February; era=y//400; yo=y−400×era; doy=(153×(m+(-3 if m>2 else 9))+2)//5+d−1; days=146097×era+365×yo+yo//4−yo//100+doy−719468. Multiply days by the D factor. Do not cast Y/M through an int64 day dtype.

For pd.Timedelta use its asm8 integer and unit factor. For datetime.timedelta use ((days×86400+seconds)×1000000+microseconds)×10^12. For fixed np.timedelta64 use its raw integer, multiplier and factor. Y/M durations have no identity key: raise TypeError, including when nested. V also currently admits unitless np.timedelta64; give these opaque keys ('timedelta64-generic',raw_integer), distinct from fixed durations. This supplies a concrete treatment without inventing a physical length or a calendar-month class. Tuples and frozensets retain their existing tagged recursive keys.

Keep refusal(), ADMITTED_TYPES and the codec unchanged. Scope fact-check: _datetime_tz_refusal at :130 currently excludes pytz-backed Python datetimes; pytz Timestamps are admitted. Under the stated outside-V non-goal, retain that exclusion. The datetime arithmetic above also works with a pytz utcoffset(), but the public key must still reject that outside-V value.

Executed evidence: a stdin-only prototype under pandas 3.0.1/NumPy 2.4.2 and pandas 2.3.3/NumPy 2.2.6 checked key equality and equal key hashes after JSON encode/decode and compressed joblib through BytesIO. All 109/109 and 111/111 keyed SAMPLES passed; the remaining two samples were the required Y/M refusals. Additional checks passed for 330 fixed-unit extreme/multiplier values, 30 Y/M datetime extremes, 192 calendar-day comparisons against NumPy, sub-ns distinctions and unit aliases. datetime.min/+23h and datetime.max/−23h produced exact aware coordinates −62135679600000000000000000000 and 253402383599999999000000000000 attoseconds. The pytz standard Timestamp, zoneinfo fold=1 Timestamp, fixed-offset codec projection and joblib projection had the same key. Codec stability follows because the saved raw coordinate/unit or datetime wall_us/offset is preserved; timezone-provider names and fold labels are not key components.

findings.title: Validate Y/M durations before any categorical cast or eligibility fallback
findings.detail:
Add a shared fit validator in category_values.py. Scan non-missing row values and every declared category, including unused declarations, recursively through exact tuple/frozenset containers. Collect the units of exact np.timedelta64 values whose np.datetime_data unit is Y or M; multipliers do not exempt them. Run this validator before identity_eligible and astype in dataframe_builder._apply_categorical, and before category learning in CategoricalEncoder.fit at lizyml/features/encoders/categorical_encoder.py:137. This prevents an unkeyable value from silently falling back to pandas and also covers direct encoder callers.

Raise LizyMLError with DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID, message "Column '<column>' contains calendar-unit numpy timedelta64 categories: <sorted units>.", and context {'column':column,'units':sorted_units,'reason':'calendar_timedelta64'}. Keep refusal()/V and encode/decode unchanged: this is a new-fit restriction, not a restriction on reading saved values. identity_eligible should require all values to be in V and contain no Y/M duration; the preceding validator supplies the fit error.

In generated train.py, validate before cast_categoricals (templates.py:306), before declared restoration (templates.py:558 and identity_template.py:314), and inside fit_pipeline before learning each column (templates.py:362), including unrestored declared values. Apply the fit restriction even when retraining an unmarked legacy configuration. Follow the scripts' existing standalone error convention: ValueError with the same column/unit message; DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID and structured context belong to the library exception API.

At predict, do not run the fit validator. A Y/M duration, including a nested one, has no key; _lookup at category_identity.py:179 and the generated lookup catch TypeError and treat it as unseen. Preserve policy behavior: mode substitutes the saved mode, nan produces missing, error raises the existing unseen-category DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID (generated scripts: ValueError). Legacy columns keep their saved pandas behavior.

Executed evidence: the prototype refused Y/M multiples, tuple/frozenset nesting and an unused declared month category. For a newly fitted string column, arrivals [Y,(M,),None,'x'] produced codes [0,0,-1,0] under mode and [-1,-1,-1,0] under nan, with two corrected rows; error named column c and both unseen values. Both generated transform copies matched these policies. On the H-0138 probe population, 221 pandas-3 columns and 225 pandas-2 columns contain Y/M. Of these, today's builder cast plus encoder fit succeeds for 203 and 211 respectively; the other 18 and 14 already fail. The two scalar samples beside 'x' fit today on both versions and become explicit refusals. Without the string companion, the individual Y/M columns fit on pandas 2 but already fail on pandas 3. The complete mixed-unit SAMPLES[np.timedelta64] column already fails its cast on both versions: pandas 3 reported unsupported unit Y; pandas 2 reported 'from_unit must be <= to_unit'. Thus refusing that mixed column is not a newly lost successful fit.

findings.title: Extend the existing faithful-cast route without requiring representative type preservation
findings.detail:
Remove holds_temporal from identity_eligible and from the public key's rejection at :541; retain V validation and the Y/M exception described above. Keep holds_temporal as an observational helper for tests and census, not a routing exclusion. Apply the same change to identity_template.py:_identity_eligible at :143 and _identity_key at :126; update the stale _holds_temporal documentation at :70. Its _key at :113 must gain every temporal branch, rather than allowing temporal values to fall into the final frozenset branch.

Carry cast_is_faithful at category_values.py:614 and its generated copy at identity_template.py:147 over unchanged. Faithfulness concerns keys, row codes, missing codes and declaration order; it does not require the raw representative's type to survive pandas normalization. Retain category_identity.py:_faithful_today/:47, _holdable/:70, _rebuilt/:79 and keyed_categories/:99. A faithful result keeps today's categories, representatives, order and mode. Otherwise keep the builder's original column and IDENTITY_OBJECT_COLUMNS marker (dataframe_builder.py:124–135); learn first representatives per key, use stable sorted(key=str) order for inferred columns or declaration order for declared columns, and choose the mode by key counts with the first category winning ties. The marker continues to name columns only; categories are learned inside each fold.

CategoricalEncoder.fit at :139 records all eligible temporal columns in identity_columns, whether rebuilt or faithful. Transform at :211 always uses keyed_codes for those saved columns. Keep comparable_values and its generated copies unchanged. Keep the existing stand-in decision at :150: rebuilt columns always use positions, and faithful columns use the estimator's needs_stand_in callback. Do not force a new blanket stand-in rule merely because a column is temporal.

Executed evidence: pandas 2 materialized homogeneous Timestamp/fold categories as datetime64[ns, America/New_York]; the proposed gate accepted them and the state held Timestamps. Homogeneous np.datetime64 day columns became Timestamp representatives on both versions—datetime64[ns] categories on pandas 2 and datetime64[s] on pandas 3—and were faithful. Their encoder states therefore hold those Timestamp representatives, with stand-ins selected by the existing LightGBM callback. On pandas 3, the corresponding homogeneous Timestamp fold categories used microsecond resolution and were also faithful. The actual datetime fold-pair model changed from codes [0,0,1] to [0,1,2]. A fold=1/fixed-offset pair at the same instant changed from [0,1,2] to [0,0,1], as Contract A requires.

The previous sub-ns summary needs qualification: full mixed batches can already receive distinct codes today. Singleton batches reproduced merged codes and, on pandas 2, a missing code, sometimes without an unseen warning; it is not universally a collapse to the mode. The keyed route consistently returned the full-batch codes for ps/fs/as singleton predictions.

findings.title: Preserve saved routing and retain the existing persistence format
findings.detail:
Keep CATEGORY_IDENTITY_VERSION=1 at category_values.py:463 and FORMAT_VERSION=5 at persistence/exporter.py:71. Do not recompute identity_columns while loading, exporting or converting a state. identity_fields at category_values.py:549, CategoricalEncoder.load_state at :303–313, loader._check_identity_markers at persistence/loader.py:210, and generated _identity_fields/_load_pipeline at identity_template.py:46 and templates.py:1552 need no behavioral change.

Consequently, a develop state whose version is 1 but whose identity_columns names only non-temporal columns keeps loading and predicting through exactly its saved routes: temporal columns remain on pandas. Unmarked states also retain pandas lookup. Newly fitting or retraining a model may select temporal columns under the redefined version 1. Preserve existing unknown-version and malformed-column-list refusals; no version 2 or migration that adds columns is needed.

Keep state_changes.py:_column_codes at :61–88: it already preserves the version and the reduced identity_columns before executing the encoder. Its learned-category and mode comparisons at :106–151 therefore acquire temporal semantics through the encoder, while legacy states retain their old comparisons. Keep _category_preflight.py:_through_joblib/:46, _encoder_through_json/:58 and state_changes/:70 unchanged; they preserve the markers. Do not replace executed code/mode comparisons with Python equality of temporal representatives.

Other persistence sites remain unchanged except the declared-comparison call described in the next finding: exporter.py:94 retains its V check; :255–272 checks every saved state through both serializers; :529 writes declared codec values; loader.py:132 decodes them. codegen/artifact_writer.py:14 and :53 copy the saved version/list, codegen/config_writer.py:111 and :141 serialize declarations and the saved version, and codegen/values.py:66 remains the codec boundary. NativeFeaturePipeline.export_state_json at pipelines_native.py:140 already copies the encoder dictionary before encoding categories/modes, so it retains version 1 and the exact saved identity_columns without a shape change.

Executed evidence: after installing the in-memory mechanism, all eight pandas-3 and fourteen pandas-2 baseline model objects retained identical predictions and warning lists. New encoder states passed both existing serializer comparisons. Twelve successful pandas-2 prototype models also preserved probabilities after compressed in-memory joblib of the model/encoder, including the temporal fixes. These establish routing and serializer behavior; actual file-based Model.export/Model.load and export_state_json writes were not run in this read-only sandbox.

findings.title: Make declared-category preflight follow the saved temporal route
findings.detail:
declared_change currently always compares raw pandas CategoricalDtype casts. That comparison becomes incorrect for newly keyed temporal declarations. Add an optional encoder argument, defaulting to None so existing direct/legacy callers retain their behavior. Select the new branch only when identity_fields(encoder) returns version 1, the column is in its saved identity_columns, and the declaration contains temporal values. Pass the refit encoder explicitly from exporter.check_category_values at :274 and exporter.warn_saved_state_changes at :152 through warn_changes at _category_preflight.py:136. Do not infer the branch from current eligibility or from version 1 alone.

For that branch, project every declared value through through_json, compare the ordered lists of identity keys, and compare the first-occurrence-per-key declaration positions used by generated _restore_declared/_rebuilt. A matching ordered key list preserves both deduplication and the codes of every learned declaration; pandas' ability to construct a raw projected dtype is irrelevant. Report a projection exception as raises, a missing key as unseen, or a changed position as codes. Keep the existing pandas comparison for all other declarations. This limits the change to H-0139's saved temporal route and preserves H-0138's non-temporal contract.

Executed evidence: scanning every constructible non-Y/M temporal probe declaration found eight false refusals on pandas 3 among 4,209 checked declarations, and none among 4,373 on pandas 2. The closed pandas-3 list is p61-92, p61-93, p61-94, p61-95, p61-96, p61-97, p61-98 and p61-103: the large np.uint64 sample beside fixed timedelta units W/D/h/m/s/ms/us or the 15m multiple. Every keyed encoder state passed joblib and JSON state_changes, but unchanged declared_change reported OverflowError after JSON. Add these eight as explicit acceptance cases; merely removing holds_temporal would leave them falsely unsaveable.

findings.title: Complete the generated-code and estimator site changes
findings.detail:
Implement the exact key, calendar-duration detector and fit validation copy in identity_template.py. Extend COPY tests in tests/test_codegen/test_h0138_identity_copy.py:54–84 to include all keyable temporal samples and nesting, and replace their blanket temporal rejection expectation with Y/M/outside-V rejection. Likewise replace tests/test_core/test_category_identity.py:68–76; retain the non-temporal equality oracle at :140 unchanged.

In templates.py, change cast_categoricals/:284, fit_pipeline/:336 and apply_declared_categories/:542 only as required for validation and temporal eligibility. Keep _restore_declared at identity_template.py:307 using key equality after dtype normalization: a declaration pandas cannot hold faithfully remains unrestored and is rebuilt by key in its declared order. Keep both encode_column functions at templates.py:444 and :1619, their comparable_values copies at :403/:1578, train transform/:504 and predict transform/:1679 dispatching by saved identity_columns. Their existing key lookup catches unkeyable Y/M arrivals and applies the selected unseen policy. Keep _load_pipeline/:1552 decoding the saved category list without upgrading it. Generated LightGBM input remains numeric codes at templates.py:1465–1475 and :1753; do not introduce pandas_categorical comparisons there.

The remaining code_paths.md sites need no algorithm changes: core/_codegen_inputs.py:101 reads original declarations; pipelines_native.py:67 selects columns named by the builder marker; pipelines_native.py:124 invokes the restored encoder; core/_model_predict.py:55 restores saved pipeline state; features/column_check.py:65 leaves categorical values to the encoder. Model.predict at core/model.py:437 does not call the builder, so fit validation must not be added there. estimators/lgbm/category_json.py:58/:72 continues to decide JSON writability from actual representatives, :99 checks only raw columns, and adapter.py:158 excludes stand-in columns before that check. The encoder's existing rebuilt short-circuit prevents constructing an invalid raw dtype. LightGBM's own category comparison and core/_tuning_identity.py:138 remain outside this change. Update docs/audits/2026-10-h0138/code_paths.md:1 with these head locations; its recorded format/version details are historical.

Executed evidence: executed the proposed standalone key inside the real generated codec namespace; all 109/111 keyable SAMPLES agreed with the runtime and survived the generated codec. Extracted actual rendered train/predict function definitions into memory: both encode_column implementations matched runtime outcomes across 360 batch/policy checks per pandas version. Generated cast/fit matched runtime categories, representatives, modes and identity_columns on 124 pandas-3 and 130 pandas-2 sample/matrix columns. Four generated cast/direct-fit refusal checks passed. Fit output streams were substituted with StringIO; no generated files were written.

findings.title: Replace blanket temporal freezing with a closed before/after overlay
findings.detail:
Keep all three committed h0138_oracle_pandas-*.json.gz files byte-for-byte unchanged. Add a separate H-0139 overlay per supported pandas version containing explicit id/before/after records and a rationale manifest. Membership must be fixed from the original oracle and the closed exceptions below, never selected by observing the implementation under test. Test that overlay IDs are unique, exactly equal the specified union, and have the expected count; every before record must equal the original oracle. Compare every unchanged temporal record with the original outcome and every changed record with its committed after outcome. Keep all non-temporal encoder/model expectations unchanged.

The closed partition is Y ∪ R ∪ S. Y contains the original temporal IDs whose inputs contain either Y/M duration sample: indices 90/91 on pandas 3, 92/93 on pandas 2. It contains 221/225 IDs. Its new outcome is {'fails_at':'fit_validation','exception':'LizyMLError','code':'DATA_SCHEMA_INVALID','context':{'column':'c','units':sorted_present_units,'reason':'calendar_timedelta64'}}. R contains precisely the IDs in the original immutable temporal_cases whose saved outcome fails_at is cast, excluding Y. It contains 190/247 IDs. Each now succeeds, uses stand_in ['c'], and has first representatives deduplicated by the specified key, stably sorted by str; forward/reverse codes are their exact key positions. Expand these finite selections into literal overlay records when committing the Proposal's fixtures; tests must assert the fixed membership independently of candidate behavior.

For pandas 3, S is exactly p22-23, p22-36, p23-35, p24-38 and p60-103. Their new forward codes are respectively [0,1,2], [0,1,2], [1,0,2], [0,1,2], [0,1,2]; reverse codes are the reversals. The first four use stand_in ['c']; p60-103 keeps its old categories and empty stand_in, correcting only reversed-batch lookup. For pandas 2, S is p22-23, p22-36, p22-40, p23-35, p23-41, p24-38, p36-41 and p62-105. Their forward codes are respectively [0,1,2], [0,1,2], [0,0,1], [1,0,2], [0,0,1], [0,1,2], [0,0,1], [0,1,2]; all except p62-105 use stand_in ['c']. Preserve first representatives under the declared rebuilding rule and commit their full typed codec values.

p24-38 is a necessary explicit case: the fixed-offset datetime denotes UTC 04:59:59.999999, while pandas stores the similarly displayed Timestamp at UTC 04:59:59. Their stored coordinates differ by 999999 microseconds. Contract A therefore separates them; do not normalize the Timestamp from its displayed wall fields.

Update _h0138_answers.py:47 to exercise the real builder route instead of its unconditional astype at :50, and report fit_validation distinctly. Leave docs/audits/2026-10-h0138/oracle/make_oracle.py:1 as the historical generator; add a separate overlay generator, not regeneration of the old oracle.

Executed evidence under PYTHONHASHSEED=0: the unmodified head reproduced all 4,620 pandas-3 and 4,845 pandas-2 temporal records exactly. The prototype changed 416=221+190+5 and 480=225+247+8, leaving 4,204 and 4,365 unchanged. All 1,584 non-temporal encoder records per environment also remained exact. SHA-256 of the ordered changed-record list, serialized with json.dumps(sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':')), was d32567a34902782c6a364ea9ce36416d20755a75c2d5fa7731885b0fa3c84cc6 for pandas 3 and 24f6d73ebfe4bce045f15d3f6a75ae89b8609ee571dfeab89fdf2a3150b7571a for pandas 2. Each record contained only id, before and after. Pandas 2.0.0 could not be executed: no compatible existing environment was available, and creating one requires writes. Its overlay count and new expectations remain unmeasured, not assumed equal to 2.3.3.

findings.title: Measure rebuilding and refusal separately from identity-column selection
findings.detail:
Use the activation event specified in the request: a temporal column is rebuilt at either the builder or encoder, or is refused for Y/M. Selecting a faithful temporal column for keyed transform is not activation. Record the union once per measured input column.

Executed evidence over the exact H-0138 probe values and training shape [*values,*values,'x'] from probe_columns.py:33–47: activation was 415/4620 temporal probe columns on pandas 3 (190 cast failures rebuilt + 4 unfaithful rebuilds + 221 Y/M refusals), and 479/4845 on pandas 2 (247 + 7 + 225). Over the entire supplied probe population, including non-temporal issue shapes, these are 415/6346 and 479/6571. The temporal faithful counts were 4205 and 4366. The one additional changed oracle case on each version is a transform-only correction and therefore does not fire this condition.

Over temporal_matrix.py:_cases at :43–123, using its actual _frame(..., n=800, seed=0) categorical column, activation was 0/15 supplied matrix columns on pandas 3 and 1/19 on pandas 2. The sole activated matrix case was 'pytz standard + zoneinfo fold 1 (same instant)', rebuilt because its categories have duplicate instant keys. There were no Y/M cases in this matrix. Repeating with each supplied value twice produced the same classification.

For the outside-sandbox full-suite census, replace the old h0138_rule temporal early return with actual builder-cast faithfulness and actual encoder keyed_categories classification. At both wrapped entries record test/node, process, call/fit identifier, column, dtype, temporal presence, Y/M units and whether present in rows or unused declarations, V eligibility, builder marker, cast result/exception, predicate result, encoder rebuilt flag, chosen identity/stand-in route, and every classification error. Classify all requested categorical dtypes, not just object columns. Report builder and encoder visit populations separately, plus their declared aggregation rule; folds are visits, not deduplicated logical columns. Record rejected attempts before the underlying fit raises, and retain columns that never reach the encoder because the builder refused them. Give n/N for rebuilt, refused and their union, with outside-V and rule_error counts visible. The current census docstring's claim that predict passes through the builder is false at this head; Model.predict delegates directly to run_predict.

findings.title: Adopt testable acceptance lists and stop after the contract is demonstrated
findings.detail:
Write H-0139 acceptance criteria in the same testable form as H-0138, replacing the old temporal non-goal for this Proposal: (1) every ADMITTED_TYPES temporal branch and nesting has the specified key or explicit Y/M rejection, with closed equal/distinct fixtures covering providers, folds, naive/aware, date/midnight, all 13 NumPy datetime units, 11 fixed duration units, multipliers, generic durations, negative coordinates, endpoints and int64 extremes; codec/generated-codec/joblib preserve every key; (2) all three oracle lanes retain their original files and pass the closed overlays, with no oracle silently skipped; (3) builder, direct encoder and generated training refuse raw/nested/unused Y/M values with the specified diagnostics, while all three predict policies follow the specified unseen behavior; (4) faithful homogeneous temporal casts retain today's normalized representatives, categories, order and mode, while every rebuilt column is selected through the builder marker and its real booster pandas_categorical entry is range(k); (5) marker propagation survives copy, sorting and outer/inner/calibration splits, and a key present only in validation never enters fitted categories; (6) runtime/generated cast, fit, declared restoration and batch/singleton prediction agree over the closed sample and matrix populations; (7) saved formats 1–4 and develop format-5 states retain their saved lookup lists, version 1 stays version 1, and unknown/malformed versions still fail; (8) every saved fold/refit state and declared comparison passes the appropriate serializer check, including the eight listed pandas-3 declarations; (9) export_state_json and all artifact/codegen conversions preserve exact markers and codec values; (10) the full-suite census records the complete populations and diagnostics above.

Fact-check the H-0136 acceptance transitions explicitly. tests/test_persistence/test_h0136_acceptance.py:158, :167, the three policies at :188 and the two containers at :211 form seven formerly refused pytz cases that should now pass the shared preflight and save/predict equivalence tests. The two month-order cases at :225 and the declared-month case at :244 instead become fit refusals; the month-based export-message test at :311 must be replaced accordingly. The large-uint64 declaration at :259 is already saveable under H-0138, not a new H-0139 rescue. Stable/control cases remain serializer-equivalence tests; newly fitted instant-equivalent categories may merge.

Executed evidence: drove the exact seven pytz fixture shapes through their fit helper with tiny three-round, three-leaf models, all three one-pytz policies included. All seven passed common export preflight with no refusal warning and preserved probabilities after compressed joblib of the refit result in BytesIO. Both month orders and the declared-month fixture produced the specified fit error. The broader baseline/prototype runs also reproduced the old joblib/json refusal kinds before the change.

Review stop criterion: stop when these closed acceptance tests, the per-lane overlays, artifact/codegen checks and full-suite census pass. Continue review only for a demonstrated violation of temporal key identity, faithful-path preservation, refusal diagnostics, leakage, runtime/generated agreement, saved routing, or actual estimator handoff. Do not reopen Contract A, introduce version 2, or expand into the tuning fingerprint, LightGBM behavior, outside-V values, H-0138's non-temporal contract or #382.

Execution limits: all measurements used the two specified environments with OMP_NUM_THREADS=4, -B and workspace PYTHONPATH; lizyml.__file__ was printed and pointed into this digest-fixed tree. The copy lacks generated lizyml/_version.py, so an in-memory version-module stub was supplied solely to import it. No repository files were edited. File-based exports/loads, generated subprocess artifacts, export_state_json writes, new gzip fixtures and the full-suite census were skipped because they require writable storage. Pandas 2.0.0 remains the explicitly unmeasured lane.
